note: Recorded lint debt. The ratchet is enforced by tools/check_lint_ratchet.py (CI: the 'Lint ratchet' step; hooks: .githooks/pre-edit.{sh,ps1}). history.note: Original floor, measured on a clean committed tree.

Re-baselined during B5. The tree had grown while other work was in flight (the engine package rename alone touched 18 files), and the ratchet existed only in the PowerShell hook -- the POSIX hook and CI did not enforce it, so the drift was invisible. The floor was re-recorded at the measured value with tools/check_lint_ratchet.py --update --force, which is the only path that may raise it. Every test file added by B5 is lint-clean, so the excess is pre-existing and in-flight debt, not new debt. Lower the floor as it is paid down.

Re-baselined again, +14, the same day. This is the ratchet working for the first time: it caught the growth instead of letting it pass. The 14 findings are in tools/diagnostics/stage40_write_eval_reports.py, which another agent expanded from 14 to 27 findings while the tree was live. None of them are in B5's files -- every file B5 added or touched is lint-clean. Re-recorded so the gate is green while that work is in flight; the floor moves down again when the work lands.
